description: Justified non-financial (or otherwise reviewed-safe) hits for sdk/test/no-float-financial-parsing.test.js. Every entry names the exact file + pattern (+ optional line) it suppresses and a REASON a human can check. Never add an entry to silence a real funds-path float parse — fix the code instead.

entries.reason: activeSlots(value): Number(value) on a small integer OWNER SLOT COUNT (1..OWNER_SLOTS_V7 == 12), not a KAS/sompi amount; the matched 'value' identifier is generic, the real domain is bounds-checked by Number.isInteger + the 1..12 range immediately after.

validateComputeBudget(value, expected, label): Number(value)/Number(expected) compare the covenant's small integer COMPUTE BUDGET (10 or 100 sig-op units, per the function's own comment), not a KAS/sompi amount. STALE ASSUMPTION corrected 2026-09-06 (rc27, Codex checkpoint 11 phase): the line moved 163 -> 185 because the R7-08 STANDARD_MASS_CAP_PRE_TOCCATA constant + its comment were inserted ABOVE it; the flagged code is byte-identical to cf4e644.

computeBudget = Number(entry.computeBudget): the per-input compute-budget field is a small integer sig-op unit count (10/100/134/...), not a KAS/sompi amount; immediately validated with Number.isInteger.

smallInt(value, field, max=1_000_000): a bounded small-integer field helper (feeBps, directionMask, destScheme, etc. — 0..max), not a KAS/sompi amount; the matched 'value' identifier is generic. Bounds-checked by Number.isInteger + the max parameter immediately after.
same smallInt() helper as line 98 — the BigInt-typed branch of the same bounded small-integer conversion.

intArg(value, field): converts a BigInt constructor argument (which CAN be a KAS/sompi amount, e.g. maxPerSpend) to a JS Number for silverc's typed Expr JSON — but ONLY after explicitly checking `value > BigInt(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)` fails closed immediately above (see the function's own comment: 'any value above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER would silently lose precision — fail closed instead'), so the conversion is EXACT/lossless by construction, not the unbounded float-parsing pattern gap G1 was about.

constructorArgsKcc20: Number(s.amount) converts a token amount (BigInt) to a JS Number for the silverc constructor-arg JSON, but ONLY after `if (s.amount > BigInt(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)) fail(...)` on the line immediately above — exact/lossless by construction, same reviewed pattern as the contract-compiler*.js intArg() helpers.

computeBudget: Number(input.computeBudget ?? 0) — a small integer sig-op unit count (the function's own comment: 'payer-supplied consistency data only'), not a KAS/sompi amount. [line renumbered 91 -> 108 -> 111 by the Codex checkpoint-7/8 doc headers; statement unchanged]

transactionIdOfRpcBody (Codex checkpoint 7/8, UX-05): computeBudget = Number(strictUint(input.computeBudget, U16_MAX, ...)) converts the node-returned per-input compute-budget field (a small integer sig-op unit count, u16, not a KAS/sompi amount) to a JS Number ONLY after strictUint proved it a safe integer within u16 — exact by construction; the consensus transaction id does not commit to it at all (rusty-kaspa hashing/tx.rs id_v1 excludes the mass commit); it is passed only so the rebuilt body is a faithful copy.

smallNonNegInt(value, field, max): Number(value) on a small bounded integer (owner-slot count / compute-budget unit), immediately validated by Number.isInteger(n) && 0 <= n <= max — not a KAS/sompi amount. Byte-identical to the reviewed helper in the non-KAS sibling core/model/compute-budget-v7.js (already allowlisted); the KAS profile was derived from it.
